key_insight: Carbon-tuned hBN-graphene alloys can sense toxic gases multimodally, with BNGr-2 best for Cl2, CO, CO2, and HCN, and BNGr-3 better for NO and NO2.
engineering_relevance: These alloys are promising low-cost platforms for chemiresistive, work-function, and optical gas sensors for pollution monitoring and industrial safety.
method: Used first-principles DFT to study gas adsorption on hBN-graphene alloys with different carbon fractions.
Evaluated adsorption energy, charge transfer, band-gap change, work-function shift, and optical response for Cl2, CO, CO2, NO, NO2, and HCN.
Compared sensing performance across BNGr-2 and BNGr-3, including recovery behavior and temperature effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports significant adsorption-induced charge transfer, ~20% work-function variation, very short recovery times (10^-1 to 10^-6 s), distinct optical spectra, and desorption of all gases from BNGr-2 by 425 K.
watch_item: Because the results are DFT-based, experimental validation is still needed to confirm selectivity, recovery times, and sensor stability under real operating conditions.
paper_title: First-Principles Investigation of Multimodal Toxic Gas Sensing in Carbon-Tuned hBN-Graphene Alloys: Chemiresistive, Work-Function, and Optical Responses
